newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone says able to finance RPR buyout.
newsitem.headline: Rhone says able to finance RPR buyout.

text.p: French drugs and chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc, which said on Thursday it was considering a buyout of its Rhone-Poulenc Rorer U.S. unit, said it would have no trouble financing the 25 billion franc transaction, which would add to earnings by the third year

Group managing director Igor Landau told Reuters the company would fund the buyout with a seven billion franc capital increase, asset sales, income from the market flotation of a new chemicals and fibre unit and from improved annual cash flow after the deal.

"For the 25 billion (that the deal should cost) there will be a capital increase of seven billion francs and the income from our strategic sales as well as the income from the sale on the market of part of the new chemicals company," Landau said in a telephone interview.
"These represent about 13 billion francs so on the 25 billion we would have 20 billion and the rest would come from improved annual cash flow," he said.
He conceded that the transaction will be "a little bit dilutive in the first year, a little less in the second and not at all, in fact to the contrary, from the third year," he said.
"The dilution is sufficiently small so that we can confirm excluding exceptional items, the 20 percent growth of our profits in 1997 and 1998," he added.
He said Rhone Poulenc stopped short of an outright offer on Thursday because under a 1990 standstill agreement, Rhone Poulenc cannot increase its holding in RPR until after July 31, 1997.
Asked whether the listing of its chemical and fibres activities as a separate entity heralded its eventual withdrawal from the field, he replied, "Absolutely not."
"In a group increasingly tilted to life sciences, it was indispensable to give men and women in these speciality chemical activities their own identity," he said.
"We do not intend to let it go. We are very confident in the potential improvement in the results of these activities."
Landau at the same time confirmed the group's intention to sell activities "which correspond to a programme begun in 1996, continued in 1997 and which will be pursued in 1998.
These actvities, he said, are those which did not match "the criteria of specialty chemicals and industry services that we want to have."
He said there were no plans to make any acquisitions in the life sciences sector.
He called the $92 per share offer to minority shareholders of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer "attractive" for them and "reasonable" for Rhone-Poulenc.

Commenting on the level of Rhone-Poulenc shares which analysts have called undervalued in comparison with other companies in the sector, Landau said the group's stronger position in the "life sciences should have a positive effect on our revaluation".
On Thursday, Rhone-Poulenc shares were up 12.5 percent at 0933 GMT.
